description: Deterministic English Analysis Quality Benchmark (30 Cases)

testCases.sentence: I have went there yesterday.
testCases.description: Present perfect with specific past temporal adverb 'yesterday' and incorrect participle 'went'

testCases.sentence: She don't like the idea.
testCases.description: Subject-verb agreement error with third-person singular 'she'

testCases.sentence: He go to university every day.
testCases.expectedCorrection: He goes to university every day.
testCases.description: Missing third-person singular '-s' verb ending

testCases.sentence: I went there yesterday.
testCases.description: Grammatically correct simple past tense

testCases.sentence: I have already been there.
testCases.description: Grammatically correct present perfect with 'already'

testCases.sentence: I haven't seen him recently.
testCases.description: Grammatically correct present perfect with unspecific temporal adverb 'recently'

testCases.sentence: I am having a strong headache today.
testCases.expectedCorrection: I have a severe headache today.
testCases.description: Grammatical but non-idiomatic phrasing (continuous stative verb + strong headache)

testCases.sentence: I am interested on astronomy.
testCases.description: Preposition collocation error (on -> in)

testCases.sentence: It depends of the weather.
testCases.description: Preposition collocation error (depends of -> depends on)

testCases.sentence: She is responsible for the project.
testCases.description: Correct adjective-preposition collocation 'responsible for'

testCases.sentence: He is very good in playing chess.
testCases.expectedCorrection: He is very good at playing chess.
testCases.description: Preposition collocation error (good in -> good at)

testCases.sentence: She has been working here since three years.
testCases.expectedCorrection: She has been working here for three years.
testCases.description: Preposition of time error with present perfect continuous (since -> for)

testCases.sentence: By the time we arrived, the train had left.
testCases.description: Correct past perfect tense sequence

testCases.sentence: I saw an European movie last night.
testCases.expectedCorrection: I saw a European movie last night.
testCases.description: Article error before consonant sound /j/ (an -> a)

testCases.sentence: She goes to school by the bus.
testCases.expectedCorrection: She goes to school by bus.
testCases.description: Incorrect article usage in transport idiom 'by bus'

testCases.sentence: The list of items are on the desk.
testCases.expectedCorrection: The list of items is on the desk.
testCases.description: Subject-verb agreement error with singular head noun 'list'

testCases.sentence: Can you tell me where is the station?
testCases.expectedCorrection: Can you tell me where the station is?
testCases.description: Inverted word order in indirect question clause

testCases.sentence: If I would have known, I would have called you.
testCases.expectedCorrection: If I had known, I would have called you.
testCases.description: Third conditional error ('would have' in condition clause instead of 'had')

testCases.sentence: I'll head out in a minute.
testCases.description: Valid natural conversational phrasal verb 'head out'

testCases.sentence: I'm gonna grab kinda a quick coffee.
testCases.description: Valid informal spoken contractions 'gonna' and 'kinda'

testCases.sentence: The colour of the car is red.
testCases.description: Valid British English spelling 'colour'

testCases.sentence: We organised a great workshop.
testCases.description: Valid British English spelling 'organised'

testCases.sentence: I will see you on next Monday.
testCases.expectedCorrection: I will see you next Monday.
testCases.description: Context-dependent redundant preposition before 'next Monday'

testCases.sentence: So I was, um, trying to explain that yesterday, but actually I didn't really understand it myself.
testCases.description: Spontaneous speech with filler 'um' and conversational rhythm

testCases.sentence: I think we should, uh, go to the store—I mean, the library first.
testCases.description: Spontaneous speech with filler 'uh' and self-correction ('I mean')

testCases.sentence: Well, you know, I was... we were thinking about visiting them next weekend.
testCases.description: Spontaneous speech with discourse marker 'you know' and false start

testCases.sentence: Like, I don't know if he's coming, but, um, we'll see soon.
testCases.description: Spontaneous speech with filler 'like', contraction 'he's', and hesitation

testCases.sentence: Um, yesterday I have seen him at the coffee shop near office.
testCases.expectedCorrection: Yesterday I saw him at the coffee shop near the office.
testCases.description: Spontaneous speech with filler 'um' containing tense error and missing article

testCases.sentence: Yeah, exactly, because when you look at it... it just makes sense.
testCases.description: Spontaneous speech with conversational pause and colloquial affirmative 'yeah'

testCases.sentence: Well, uh, the people in the office is working very hard today.
testCases.expectedCorrection: The people in the office are working very hard today.
testCases.description: Spontaneous speech with filler 'uh' containing subject-verb agreement error ('people... is')
